paragraphs: Two layers, from examples/26. Drogon's HttpClient takes a timeout on every request, and sendRequestCoro suspends the coroutine handler while it waits, so a slow backend never holds an event-loop thread. A timeout or a refused connection arrives as HttpException and is reported as no answer. The deadline endpoint passes the remaining budget both as the request timeout and in the X-Deadline-Ms header, so the backend can refuse work it cannot finish.

ops.repl: Retry in a coroutine: exponential backoff + jitter, waits that suspend instead of block.

paragraphs: No maintained C++ resilience library is on ConanCenter, so the retry is a short loop in a Drogon coroutine handler. Three attempts at most; between them the wait starts at 100 ms, doubles up to 2 seconds and gets up to half again as jitter. The wait is co_await sleepCoro, which suspends the handler instead of blocking the event-loop thread. Retry only idempotent calls, and pair the retry with a circuit breaker.

paragraphs: The breaker from examples/26, written in the service because no maintained C++ resilience library is on ConanCenter. One mutex guards three states: five consecutive failures open it, the first call after ten seconds moves it to half-open, two successful trials close it and one failed trial opens it again. The handler asks allow() before calling the backend and records the outcome afterwards; when allow() refuses, it answers from the fallback with circuit_open.
